speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly where in your neck and arm the pain is located, and does it radiate in any specific direction? Also, could you tell me when these symptoms first started?

text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. speaker: Doctor
text: Could you specify if the weakness and numbness affect all fingers or just the thumb, index, and middle fingers, and do you notice any loss of fine motor skills like buttoning a shirt? Also, does the pain worsen when you hold your arms up or turn your neck?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of fasciculations and absent reflexes suggests potential lower motor neuron involvement, so I need to clarify if this weakness is symmetrical and if you've noticed any muscle wasting in your shoulders or neck. Do you experience any difficulty walking, balance issues, or changes in bowel and bladder control? REQUEST TEST: EMG and Nerve Conduction Studies.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the MRI finding of a syrinx extending from the cervical to upper thoracic region alongside your "cape-like" sensory loss and lower motor neuron signs, I have sufficient evidence. DIAGNOSIS READY: Syringomyelia.
